label: Legal-expenses insurance: cover confirmation, refusal, and the disagreement procedure

contract.scope: Legal-expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung) under a Swiss private policy, instantiated on a tenancy dispute: the insured notifies a legal matter; the insurer establishes cover, issues or refuses a cost undertaking (Kostengutsprache); on a refusal for lack of prospects it must give written reasons and point to the contractual disagreement procedure; the insured then invokes that procedure, accepts, or self-funds with a right of retrospective reimbursement. The contract is bounded by the supervisory spine (AVO Art. 161-170, SR 961.011, Stand 1.1.2026; VAG Art. 32, SR 961.01, Stand 1.9.2024), the mandatory/dispositive claims rules of the VVG (SR 221.229.1, Stand 1.1.2024, as carried in swiss-authority-bundle-v1.json), and seven independent published private legal-expenses general-conditions families (Generali/Fortuna 02.2024, Dextra Flex 05.2022, Orion Private 01/2022, Orion-for-HEV, Protekta/Mobiliar 01.2026, AXA-ARAG 2021, Coop AVBPP24, Assista/TCS 2011 Ausgabe 09.2023), plus two operational sources (Protekta "Rechtsfall melden" page; CAP Checkliste ZRRP505D-0219) and the Ombudsman Reglement 2026 for the one routing predicate that closes an onward route. NOT in scope: insurer-internal intake, triage, reserving and allocation; the method of assessing prospects of success; the field structure of a tenancy claim form (no public one exists). terminals: Cover confirmed and a Kostengutsprache issued, possibly limited in amount, time, conditions and procedural stage, so that the insured carries no cost risk within those limits (Generali C2 Art. 4; Orion E5(2); CAP checklist). The checklist's own qualification applies: an appeal to the next instance is not automatically covered.

Refusal for lack of prospects, reasoned in writing and accompanied by the pointer to the disagreement procedure, which the insured accepts: the matter closes and the insured himself carries responsibility for appeal, forfeiture and limitation periods (AVO 169(2); Generali C3 Art. 1: 'Die Wahrung von Rechtsmittel-, Verwirkungs- und Verjaehrungsfristen obliegt in diesem Fall der versicherten Person.').
The disagreement procedure is held and the single arbitrator or independent expert determines the measure, with the costs borne by the losing party (AVO 169(1); Orion E6(2); AXA-ARAG A9).

Deemed waiver: the contractual window elapsed without a demand for the procedure, and the wording treats this as a renunciation (Orion E6(1); Protekta M8; AXA-ARAG A9; Generali C3 Art. 2). Not available under the Coop family, which fixes no window.

Deemed recognition: the contract provides no AVO 169(1) procedure, or the insured was not informed of it at the moment liability was declined, so the need for legal protection counts as recognised in that case (AVO 169(3)) - a procedural omission by the insurer converting directly into cover.

Self-funded litigation with a result more favourable than the insurer's written reasoned solution or than the outcome of the procedure: the insurer assumes the resulting costs up to the maximum of the sum insured (AVO 169(4); Generali C3 Art. 3; Orion E6(3); Protekta M7; Coop 14).
Cost-advance default inside the disagreement procedure: the defaulting party is treated as accepting the other party's legal view (Orion E6(1)).

Forfeiture of the insurance claim for failure to make the communications or produce the files within the period set in writing under warning of default (VVG 39(2)(2); Generali C1 Art. 2, where the insurer is released from the obligation to perform; Orion-for-HEV, where the insurance claim lapses).

Reduction or refusal of benefits for culpable breach of an obligation, unless the breach was blameless or is proved to have had no influence on the event or on the extent of the benefits (VVG 38(2), 45(1); Protekta M4; AXA-ARAG A8; Coop 12; Assista 16).
The insurer is not bound by the contract at all, where facts excluding or reducing liability were misstated or concealed for the purpose of deception (VVG 40).
Prozessauskauf: the insurer discharges itself by replacing the economic interest in whole or in part instead of rendering the insured services (Orion E5(3); Protekta M6; AXA-ARAG A8).

The claim is time-barred five years after the fact founding the obligation (VVG 46(1)); any shorter contractual limitation or time restriction is invalid save for the single reserved case (VVG 46(2)).

Escalation to the neutral Ombudsman of private insurance - open only while the applicant is not and has not been professionally represented by a lawyer or a legal-expenses insurer, and while the claim is not already time-barred or forfeited; filing is by the Beschwerdeformular by post or online (Ombudsman Reglement 2026). A confirmed legal-expenses mandate therefore closes this terminal on the same file.
